items.text: What do systematic reviews published from 2017 show about the effects of link worker social prescribing on wellbeing, loneliness, primary care consultations and costs in adults, once review quality and overlap of primary studies are taken into account?
items.population: Adults referred to link worker social prescribing, as included in systematic reviews
items.intervention: Social prescribing delivered through a link worker
items.comparator: Usual care or no referral, as defined in the reviews
items.outcome: Wellbeing, loneliness, primary care consultations and costs, each graded separately

finer: Feasible from published reviews with two sessions a week; interesting to commissioners and link workers; novel in counting primary studies once; ethical with no patient data; relevant to a funding decision.
summary: One overview question with outcomes graded separately.
